newsitem.title: USA: Texas doctor cleared in cancer drug case. [CORRECTED 01:02 GMT 18/5]
newsitem.headline: Texas doctor cleared in cancer drug case. [CORRECTED 01:02 GMT 18/5]

text.p: A doctor accused of ignoring a judicial order to stop selling a non-approved cancer drug was found not guilty on Tuesday by a federal jury.

The verdict likely ended 14 years of legal battles in which physician Stanislaw Burzynski fended off dozens of federal charges linked to the sale of "antineoplastons" -- a drug he created from human and animal urine.
"It's the end of 14 years of war. It's a great day for us," Burzynski told reporters after the verdict.
Burzynski's problems began when he started selling the drug without Food and Drug Administration approval (corrects name of the agency).

Now it is being tested under FDA guidelines, but its efficacy is not yet known. Burzynski's patients, convinced of the drug's ability to heal, have rallied to his side throughout the legal fight and applauded as he left the courthouse after the verdict.

"It means medical freedom for all of us," Mary Jo Siegel of Pacific Palisades, Calif., said of the verdict. She said she began taking antineoplastons in 1992 after other doctors told her she would die shortly of cancer. She is now cured.

Burzynski was tried earlier this year on 75 counts of fraud, unauthorised drug sales and contempt of court, but a jury in February deadlocked 6-6 on whether to convict. All but the contempt charge were dismissed or dropped before the latest trial, which began on May 20.
Burzynski's lawyers portrayed him as a victim of government persecution and declared the not-guilty verdict a victory for those opposed to government intrusion.
But federal prosecutor Mike Clarke said the government's concern was for the patients taking an unproven drug.
"We didn't want a pound of flesh. We just wanted accountability," he told Reuters.
